links.note: The one's digit of 53 cubed is 7 because 3 taken three times is 27. The work is cubing the last digit - a number multiplied by itself three times - since parity alone (31360) leaves all four odd options standing.
243 is the non-cube against 216, 1000 and 1331. This concept names 243 explicitly: grouping its factors in triplets leaves a stray 3 x 3.
Cube root of 512 is 8 - asking what number cubed gives 512, i.e. undoing the cubing. 512 is small enough that no factorisation into triples is needed.
4 times the cube root of 1000 is 4 x 10 = 40; the only step that is not arithmetic is inverting the cubing to get 10.
A cube's zeros come in threes because the factor 10 must appear three times over, so 2 trailing zeros is impossible. That is the each-prime-factor-three-times structure, applied to the factors of 10.
4 cubed = 64: the number taken three times, which is what the word cube names.
5 cubed = 125 by multiplying 5 by itself three times.
The cube of an odd number is odd - stated word for word in this concept alongside the count of cubes up to 1000.

Identifies 1729 among near neighbours. What makes 1729 the Hardy-Ramanujan number is its being the smallest sum of two cubes in two ways, which is this concept; 31355 is the taxi anecdote rather than the number's defining property.
392 = 2 cubed x 7 x 7, so one more 7 completes the triple and gives 2744. This concept's own worked example.
243 = 3^5, so multiplying by 3 gives 3^6 = 729, a cube. The smallest multiplier is whatever completes the incomplete group of threes.
a cubed expands to a x a x a - the definition of taking a number three times, against distractors that add it three times or multiply by 3.
A number ending in 2 cubes to one ending in 8, because 2 taken three times is 8. Cubing the last digit is the whole calculation.
729 is 9 cubed; the options are settled by cubing 8, 9, 6 and 4 in turn.
125 is the cube among 135, 145 and 115, all of which leave stray factors when grouped in triplets (135 = 3 cubed x 5). Factorisation is what separates them.
Cube root of 512 is 8 - the same inverse-of-cubing question as qid 113613, with different distractors.
9 is the cube root of 729, read as 9 cubed = 729. The inverse relation between cubing and taking a cube root is the whole of it.
27000 = 3 cubed x 10 cubed, so the root is 30 with one zero. Taking one factor from each group of three is what turns three zeros into one.
Cube root of 343 is 7: what number cubed gives 343.
The cube root of 216 is the single digit 6, so its unit digit is 6. The question reduces to inverting the cubing.
15625 = 5^6, which groups into two triples of 5 and gives the root 25, unit digit 5. At this size the factors have to be grouped in threes rather than the cube recognised.
Gives 8 cubed = 512 and asks for the cube root of 512 - the inverse relation stated in the stem and applied in the answer.
108 = 2 x 2 x 3 cubed leaves a stray 2 x 2 after grouping in triplets, while 216, 343 and 125 group cleanly. The leftovers decide it.
